reply:
They're the same storage type in Postgres, both varlena, so read performance is identical. The choice between VARCHAR(2000) and TEXT is about whether you want the database to enforce the 2000-byte limit on write—not performance.

If you need the constraint, use VARCHAR(2000). If the length is truly unbounded and you don't need enforcement, TEXT is fine. Performance is a wash either way.

grade.note: Assistant retracts fixed-width claim and correctly states varlena storage is identical, differing only by length enforcement.
